On March 25th, 2026, we published our third Python package,
[Flower](https://pypi.org/project/seedcase-flower), to PyPI. This package
converts a data package's structured, machine-readable metadata to something
more suited to humans, for example as a website. This is one of our first
packages that non-data engineer people might interact with and use (compared to
our other two packages, [Sprout](https://sprout.seedcase-project.org) or
[`check-datapackge`](https://check-datapackage.seedcase-project.org)). The
output of Flower is (ideally) one of the first ways that researchers interact
with a data package from a research study.

## What is Flower?

[Flower's dedicated website](https://check-datapackage.seedcase-project.org) has
more details about it, but very simply, Flower is a command-line tool that takes
a metadata file, like [`datapackage.json`](https://datapackage.org), and
converts it into human-readable files like Markdown. These Markdown files can
than be used to convert into HTML or PDF files, for easier sharing with
researchers or those who may use the data in the data package. We hope that
Flower will help with the issue that researchers frequently face when working
with data: lack of documentation about what the data they're working on means.

## Why use it?

Aligning with our general principles of keeping tools simple and focused, we
kept Flower sharply focused on output a human-readable document from
machine-readable metadata. It's also highly customisable, so if our current
styles don't fit your needs, you aren't restricted. We will also continue to add
more styles and improve on the existing ones.

What to see what some of those styles look like? [Check out our "Examples"
page](https://flower.seedcase-project.org/docs/examples/)!

## Commands in Flower

There are (so far) two commands in Flower: `build` and `view`. You can run it
fairly easily with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to see the help docs for
them:

```bash
uvx seedcase-flower
```

`build` is the core of the package, which is what will actually convert the
metadata into something human-friendly:

```bash
uvx seedcase-flower build --help
```

`view` is a command to quickly view the metadata if the owner of the data
package hasn't yet made a website but have used some type of metadata file like
`datapackage.json`:

```bash
uvx seedcase-flower view --help
```

We do have some plans to make a more interact terminal-based viewer for those
more advanced users.
